name: Alderwick Manor
blurbs: A country house, a reading of the will, and one guest who never came down to supper.
Rain against the windows, a fire in every grate, and a family that cannot agree on anything.
Everyone came for the anniversary. Someone came for something else.
The clocks were wound, the silver polished, and by morning the house had a new heir.
The family has gathered for a birthday. By the end of the evening, it has one member fewer.
Fog over the lawns, a cold supper and a butler who saw more than anyone should.
An old feud, a new will and a long night when every door in the house was locked.
The guests dressed for dinner. One of them dressed for murder.
Three generations under one roof, and not one of them willing to leave before the lawyers do.
The invitations promised a quiet weekend. The host had other plans, and so did somebody else.
A portrait has gone missing, the port has gone round, and one guest has gone for good.
Everyone at dinner smiled at the announcement. One of them had already decided to stop it.
motives: the will had been rewritten that very morning
an old debt of honour had finally come due
a letter had turned up in the wrong drawer
the family silver was not quite as silver as it looked
a forty-year-old wager was about to be settled
the family portrait had been painted over someone's face
a quiet engagement would have cut three cousins out of the estate
the deeds to the house had been gambled away twice
the gamekeeper's confession had been kept in a locked box for years
the heir was not, strictly speaking, an heir
a long-lost brother had written to say he was on his way home
the butler's savings had paid for the new roof, and nobody had said thank you
a secret marriage had been recorded in the parish register
the dowager's diamonds had been sold decades ago and replaced with glass
a blackmail letter had arrived with the morning post, in a familiar hand
epilogues: {murderer} and {victim} were alone in the {area}. Nobody else saw a thing, which was rather the point: {motive}.
Only {murderer} was in the {area} with {victim}. The rest of the house was busy being innocent, and {murderer} knew it: {motive}.
The {area} held two people that evening, and one of them walked out. {murderer} had a reason: {motive}.
Supper was cold by the time anyone thought to look in the {area}. {murderer} had counted on it: {motive}.
Two went into the {area} and the house heard only one come out. {murderer} never did explain the mud on those shoes, but the reason was plain enough: {motive}.
{victim} had asked for a quiet word in the {area}. {murderer} obliged, because {motive}.
The family blamed the draught, the dog and each other. Only {murderer} had shared the {area} with {victim}, because {motive}.
By the time the gong sounded, {murderer} had left the {area} and straightened the pictures. As for why: {motive}.
